q_en: How does a modern story show what is seen, what is thought, what is felt and what is said, all in one passage?
q_ar: كَيْفَ تَجْمَعُ الْقِصَّةُ الْحَدِيثَةُ بَيْنَ الْوَصْفِ وَالْفِكْرِ وَالشُّعُورِ وَالْكَلَامِ فِي نَصٍّ وَاحِدٍ؟
not_yet: Every kind of modern prose: stories, essays and novels each have their own habits.
Long literary sentences with many clauses: you read the first clauses of one.
The Arabic of dialogue in the streets: stories often write it in fuṣḥā, and you read it so.
not_yet_ar: كُلُّ أَنْوَاعِ النَّثْرِ الْحَدِيثِ: لِلْقِصَّةِ وَالْمَقَالَةِ وَالرِّوَايَةِ عَادَاتٌ مُخْتَلِفَةٌ.
الْجُمَلُ الْأَدَبِيَّةُ الطَّوِيلَةُ: تَقْرَأُ هُنَا أَوَّلَهَا فَقَطْ.
كَلَامُ النَّاسِ فِي الشَّارِعِ: تَكْتُبُهُ الْقِصَّةُ غَالِبًا بِالْفُصْحَى.

slides.head_en: Look: four ways a story speaks
slides.head_ar: اُنْظُرْ: أَرْبَعُ طُرُقٍ تَتَكَلَّمُ بِهَا الْقِصَّةُ
sents: كَانَ الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلًا وَكَانَ الصَّمْتُ كَبِيرًا.
The road was long and the silence was great.
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ فِي نَفْسِهِ: هَلْ أُمِّي فِي الْبَيْتِ الْآنَ؟
Ahmad said to himself: Is my mother at home now?
جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ.
Ahmad sat, looking at the sea.
قَالَ لَهُ أَبُوهُ: لِمَاذَا لَا تَتَكَلَّمُ؟
His father said to him: Why do you not speak?

lines: Which sentence does nobody hear? Which words tell you?

In sentence 3 the boy does two things at once. Which words show the second thing?
فِي الْجُمْلَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ يَفْعَلُ الْوَلَدُ شَيْئَيْنِ مَعًا. أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تُظْهِرُ الشَّيْءَ الثَّانِيَ؟
Sentence 1 has no action at all. What does it do for the story?
لَيْسَ فِي الْجُمْلَةِ الْأُولَى حَدَثٌ. مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ لِلْقِصَّةِ؟

cards.def_en: كَانَ, a noun and its description: the road, the silence, the sun.
The words nobody hears: his thoughts.
A second thing at the same moment: “as he looks”, “as she prays”.

slides.tip: A modern story rarely names the feeling. It shows what the person does, and you read the feeling.
slides.tip_ar: الْقِصَّةُ الْحَدِيثَةُ لَا تُسَمِّي الشُّعُورَ غَالِبًا، بَلْ تُرِيكَ مَا يَفْعَلُهُ الشَّخْصُ.

slides.head_en: Little words that carry the story
rows: one thing happens, and straight after it another
slides.note: In وَمَا إِنْ … حَتَّى the first half is a short event and the second half is what follows at once.
slides.note_ar: فِي «وَمَا إِنْ … حَتَّى» يَأْتِي الْحَدَثُ الْأَوَّلُ ثُمَّ يَتْبَعُهُ الثَّانِي مُبَاشَرَةً.

lines: خَرَجَتِ السَّيَّارَةُ مِنْ تَرِيمَ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ،
The car left Tarim after the dawn,
وَجَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ قُرْبَ الْبَابِ وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الطَّرِيقِ.
and Ahmad sat near the door, looking at the road.
كَانَ الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلًا، وَكَانَ الصَّمْتُ كَبِيرًا فِي السَّيَّارَةِ،
The road was long, the silence in the car was great,
وَكَانَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ وَاضِحَةً.
and the sun was clear above the mountain.
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ فِي نَفْسِهِ: «هَلْ أُمِّي فِي الْبَيْتِ الْآنَ؟»
Ahmad said to himself: “Is my mother at home now?”
خرجت السيارة من تريم بعد الفجر،
وجلس أحمد قرب الباب وهو ينظر إلى الطريق.
كان الطريق طويلًا، وكان الصمت كبيرًا في السيارة،
وكانت الشمس فوق الجبل واضحةً.
قال أحمد في نفسه: «هل أمي في البيت الآن؟»

slides.why: فِي نَفْسِهِ means “to himself”: a thought nobody hears. To speak to another person, write قَالَ لَهُ.
slides.why_ar: «فِي نَفْسِهِ» لِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُهُ أَحَدٌ. وَلِلْكَلَامِ مَعَ شَخْصٍ نَقُولُ: «قَالَ لَهُ».

slides.head_en: A real story: a king on the shore
lines: فَأَلْقَى عَلَى مُلْكِهِ الذَّاهِبِ نَظْرَةً طَوِيلَةً
He cast a long look at his departing kingdom,
لَمْ يَسْتَرْجِعْهَا إِلَّا مُبَلَّلَةً بِالدَّمْعِ،
which he took back only drenched in tears,
ثُمَّ أَدْنَى رِدَاءَهُ مِنْ وَجْهِهِ
then he drew his cloak up to his face
وَأَنْشَأَ يَبْكِي بُكَاءً مُرًّا …
and began to weep bitterly …

sections.name: A
sections.en: A text. Read it, then answer.
lines: خَرَجَتِ السَّيَّارَةُ مِنْ تَرِيمَ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ، وَجَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ قُرْبَ الْبَابِ وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الطَّرِيقِ.
The car left Tarim after the dawn, and Ahmad sat near the door, looking at the road.
كَانَ الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلًا، وَكَانَ الصَّمْتُ كَبِيرًا فِي السَّيَّارَةِ، وَكَانَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ وَاضِحَةً.
The road was long, the silence in the car was great, and the sun was clear above the mountain.
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ فِي نَفْسِهِ: «هَلْ أُمِّي فِي الْبَيْتِ الْآنَ؟»
Ahmad said to himself: “Is my mother at home now?”
ثُمَّ جَاءَتْ إِلَيْهِ ذِكْرَى الْبَيْتِ: الْخُبْزُ فِي الْمَطْبَخِ، وَأُمُّهُ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ تَدْعُو لَهُ.
Then a memory of home came to him: the bread in the kitchen, and his mother at the door praying for him.
وَكَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ شُعُورٌ جَدِيدٌ: لَا هُوَ حَزِينٌ وَلَا هُوَ سَعِيدٌ.
And in his heart was a new feeling: he was neither sad nor happy.
قَالَ لَهُ أَبُوهُ وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ: «لِمَاذَا لَا تَتَكَلَّمُ يَا بُنَيَّ؟»
His father said to him, looking at him: “Why do you not speak, my son?”
فَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: «أَنَا أَتَذَكَّرُ الْبَيْتَ يَا أَبِي.»
Ahmad said: “I am remembering the house, Father.”
ثُمَّ قَالَ الْأَبُ: «وَهَذَا طَيِّبٌ، فَكُلُّ مُسَافِرٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ بَيْتَهُ.»
Then the father said: “That is good, for every traveller remembers his home.”
وَمَا إِنْ نَزَلَتِ السَّيَّارَةُ مِنَ الْجَبَلِ حَتَّى رَأَى الْبَحْرَ أَمَامَهُ.
No sooner had the car come down from the mountain than he saw the sea before him.

وَفِي الْمَسَاءِ نَزَلُوا فِي الشِّحْرِ، فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ رِسَالَةً إِلَى أُمِّهِ: «رَأَيْتُ الْبَحْرَ الْيَوْمَ يَا أُمِّي، وَتَذَكَّرْتُ بَيْتَنَا.» ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فِي صَمْتٍ جَمِيلٍ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ.
In the evening they stopped in al-Shiḥr, and Ahmad wrote a letter to his mother: “I saw the sea today, Mother, and I remembered our home.” Then he sat in a beautiful silence and looked at the sea.

items.en: Which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A modern short story. Clues: it tells events in the past; it describes (كَانَ الطَّرِيقُ …); it gives the boy’s thoughts (قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ); and it quotes spoken lines between « ».

items.en: Where does the story begin, and at what time of day?
items.ar_q: أَيْنَ تَبْدَأُ الْقِصَّةُ؟ وَفِي أَيِّ وَقْتٍ؟
options: The road (long), the silence in the car (great), and the sun
“Neither sad nor happy”: a new, mixed feeling
In the car leaving Tarim, after the dawn
items.answer: In the car leaving Tarim, after the dawn
items.model: In the car leaving Tarim, after the dawn (الْفَجْرِ).

items.en: Which words tell what Ahmad was doing while he sat? Translate them.
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَقُولُ مَاذَا كَانَ يَفْعَلُ أَحْمَدُ وَهُوَ جَالِسٌ؟ تَرْجِمْهَا.
items.model: وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الطَّرِيقِ: “looking at the road”. It is a state clause (حَالٌ).

items.en: Line 2 describes three things. Name them.
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٢ يَصِفُ ثَلَاثَةَ أَشْيَاءَ. اُذْكُرْهَا.
options: In the car leaving Tarim, after the dawn
“Neither sad nor happy”: a new, mixed feeling
The road (long), the silence in the car (great), and the sun
items.answer: The road (long), the silence in the car (great), and the sun
items.model: The road (long), the silence in the car (great), and the sun (clear above the mountain).

items.en: To whom is Ahmad speaking in line 3? How do you know?
items.ar_q: لِمَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ أَحْمَدُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: To himself: فِي نَفْسِهِ means “in himself”, a thought that nobody hears.

items.en: What came to Ahmad in line 4? Name the two pictures.
items.ar_q: مَاذَا جَاءَ إِلَى أَحْمَدَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤؟ اُذْكُرْ صُورَتَيْنِ.
items.model: A memory of home: the bread in the kitchen, and his mother at the door, praying for him.

items.ar: لَا هُوَ حَزِينٌ وَلَا هُوَ سَعِيدٌ
items.en: Translate. What kind of feeling is this?
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمْ. مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا الشُّعُورِ؟
options: In the car leaving Tarim, after the dawn
“Neither sad nor happy”: a new, mixed feeling
The road (long), the silence in the car (great), and the sun
items.answer: “Neither sad nor happy”: a new, mixed feeling
items.model: “Neither sad nor happy”: a new, mixed feeling (شُعُورٌ جَدِيدٌ).

items.en: What does the father ask, and what does Ahmad answer?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَسْأَلُ الْأَبُ؟ وَبِمَاذَا يُجِيبُ أَحْمَدُ؟
items.model: He asks why Ahmad does not speak. Ahmad answers that he is remembering the house.

items.ar: وَمَا إِنْ نَزَلَتِ السَّيَّارَةُ مِنَ الْجَبَلِ حَتَّى رَأَى الْبَحْرَ
items.en: Translate the pattern وَمَا إِنْ … حَتَّى …
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمْ هَذَا الْأُسْلُوبَ.
items.model: No sooner had the car come down from the mountain than he saw the sea.

items.en: Put these in order: (a) he saw the sea (b) the father spoke about travellers (c) the car left Tarim (d) he wrote to his mother.
items.ar_q: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) رَأَى الْبَحْرَ (ب) تَكَلَّمَ الْأَبُ عَنِ الْمُسَافِرِينَ (ج) خَرَجَتِ السَّيَّارَةُ (د) كَتَبَ إِلَى أُمِّهِ.
options: The road (long), the silence in the car (great), and the sun
In the car leaving Tarim, after the dawn
“Neither sad nor happy”: a new, mixed feeling
items.model: c, b, a, d.

items.en: ★ The story never says “Ahmad missed his home”. How do we learn it?
items.ar_q: ★ لَا تَقُولُ الْقِصَّةُ «اشْتَاقَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ». كَيْفَ عَرَفْنَا؟
items.model: From what he thinks, remembers and does: the inner speech, the memory of the bread, his silence, the letter. The writer shows the feeling and does not name it.

items.en: ★ In line 2 the silence is “great”; in the last line it is “beautiful” (صَمْتٍ جَمِيلٍ). What has changed in the story?
items.ar_q: ★ الصَّمْتُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ «كَبِيرٌ» وَفِي الْآخِرِ «جَمِيلٌ». مَاذَا تَغَيَّرَ؟
items.model: At first the silence is a weight between father and son. At the end Ahmad has spoken, understood his feeling and written to his mother, so the silence has become peaceful.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A real story, written about a hundred years ago: a king stands on the shore after losing his city. Read it, then answer.
lines: فَأَلْقَى عَلَى مُلْكِهِ الذَّاهِبِ نَظْرَةً طَوِيلَةً لَمْ يَسْتَرْجِعْهَا إِلَّا مُبَلَّلَةً بِالدَّمْعِ،
He cast a long look at his departing kingdom, which he took back only drenched in tears,
ثُمَّ أَدْنَى رِدَاءَهُ مِنْ وَجْهِهِ وَأَنْشَأَ يَبْكِي بُكَاءً مُرًّا …
then he drew his cloak up to his face and began to weep bitterly …
sections.source: Muṣṭafā Luṭfī al-Manfalūṭī, al-ʿAbarāt, the story «الذكرى» (al-Dhikrā)
sections.cite: Muṣṭafā Luṭfī al-Manfalūṭī (1876–1924), al-ʿAbarāt, 'al-Dhikrā' (a story adapted from the French: «مترجمة» in the copy), first published 1916 (public domain); text read in the Shamela Master Library copy [32980] 'العبرات للمنفلوطي' (Hodeidah 3.64 copy; edition and imprint not given), digital page 55. No print was found, so NO PRINTED PAGE and no edition claim. The copy's beginning of «اليتيم» is missing (it starts mid-sentence), so this opening of «الذكرى» is used; «الحجاب» was rejected (cultural polemic against Europe). Used here: the first part of the second sentence only (up to «بُكَاءً مُرًّا»; the sentence goes on in the source), as two lines; the vowels are the course's (vowelled for learners).

items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A modern literary story of the early twentieth century (al-Manfalūṭī, «الذكرى»). It paints a feeling through what the king does and sees.

items.en: Translate line 1.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
items.model: He cast a long look at his departing kingdom, which he took back only drenched in tears,

items.en: Translate line 2.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: then he drew his cloak up to his face and began to weep bitterly …

items.en: What did the king do, and at what? Name the word for “look”.
items.ar_q: مَاذَا فَعَلَ الْمَلِكُ؟ وَإِلَى مَاذَا نَظَرَ؟
items.model: He cast a long look (نَظْرَةً) at his departing kingdom (مُلْكِهِ الذَّاهِبِ).

items.en: What did he do with his cloak, and why do you think he did it?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا فَعَلَ بِرِدَائِهِ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
items.model: He drew it up to his face, to hide his weeping.

items.en: The verb and the noun share a root. What is it? What does the second word add?
items.ar_q: الْفِعْلُ وَالِاسْمُ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ. مَا هُوَ؟ وَمَاذَا تَزِيدُ الْكَلِمَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ؟

items.en: What is wrong with the ending?
items.ar_q: مَا الْخَطَأُ؟
items.model: After the little word إِلَى the noun must end in kasra: إِلَى الْبَحْرِ.

items.en: What is wrong with the state clause?
items.ar_q: مَا الْخَطَأُ؟
items.model: The pronoun must agree with the doer. Maryam is “she”, so: وَهِيَ سَعِيدَةٌ.

items.en: What is wrong with the verb?
items.ar_q: مَا الْخَطَأُ؟
items.model: ذِكْرَى (“memory”) is feminine, so the verb must be feminine: جَاءَتْ ذِكْرَى الْبَيْتِ.

ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
pvnnnnnvnn
Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.
قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
vnnnpnvn
Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.
قَالَتْ: اللَّهُ مَوْجُودٌ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ.
vnnnn
She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا.
vnnpnpnnnnp
The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.
وَعَلَيْكَ بِصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَبِالْوَفَاءِ بِالْوَعْدِ.
pnnnn
And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى.
vnnnpn
The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness).
وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
nppnnpnpnnp
And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.
قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ وَحَضَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَهُمْ.
vnnnpnvnp
The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them.
وَقَالُوا: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ثَلَاثًا.
vvnnnpnnvn
And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
pnnvnnpn
On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque.
وَقَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ الْمَوْلِدَ وَذَكَرُوا جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
vnnvnnpn
And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
vnpnnpnnp
The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
وَفِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ صَدْرٌ وَعَجُزٌ.
pnnnn
And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: وُلِدَ فِي مَكَّةَ وَنَشَأَ يَتِيمًا وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
vnnnpvpnvnvn
The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care.
فَأَحَبَّ الْوَلَدُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ أَكْثَرَ.
vnnpn
So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً مِنْ رَسَائِلِ الْإِمَامِ.
vnnpnn
The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam.
وَكَانَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا: وَبَعْدُ، وَفِي آخِرِهَا: وَالسَّلَامُ.
vpnppnn
At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا.
vnnnpnpnnnn
The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision.
وَكَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ.
vnnvvnp
And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.
سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَبِيعَ الرَّجُلُ الرُّطَبَ فِي السُّوقِ؟
vnpvpvnnpn
Fatima asked: Is it allowed for a man to sell fresh dates in the market?
سُئِلَ الْحَبِيبُ فَأَجَابَ: نَعَمْ، يَجُوزُ.
vnvpv
The Habib was asked, and he answered: Yes, it is allowed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَتْنِ عَنِ الْإِعْرَابِ: وَأَقْسَامُهُ أَرْبَعَةٌ: رَفْعٌ وَنَصْبٌ وَخَفْضٌ وَجَزْمٌ.
vnpnpnnnnnnn
The boy read in the matn about iʿrāb: Its kinds are four: rafʿ, naṣb, khafḍ and jazm.
وَعَرَفَ الْوَلَدُ أَنَّ الضَّمَّةَ عَلَامَةُ الرَّفْعِ.
vnpnnn
And the boy knew that the ḍamma is the sign of rafʿ.
اِسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى تَسْجِيلِ دَرْسٍ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
vnpnnpn
The boy listened to a recording of a lesson by the Habib.
وَفَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ كُلَّهُ.
vnnnn
And the boy understood all the words of the Habib.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْأَخْبَارِ: نَزَلَتِ الْأَمْطَارُ فِي الْوَادِي.
vnpnvnpn
The boy heard on the news: Rain fell in the wadi.
وَأُعْلِنَ أَنَّ الْمَطَرَ غَزِيرٌ جِدًّا.
vpnnn
And it was announced that the rain was very heavy.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً إِلَى بَيْتِهِ.
vnnpn
The boy wrote a letter home.
وَكَتَبَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا تَحِيَّةً لِأُمِّهِ وَفِي آخِرِهَا تَوْقِيعَهُ.
vpnnnpnn
He wrote at its beginning a greeting to his mother, and at its end his signature.
خَلَطَتْ فَاطِمَةُ الدَّقِيقَ وَالْمَاءَ وَالْمِلْحَ فِي إِنَاءٍ كَبِيرٍ.
vnnnnpnn
Fatima mixed the flour, the water and the salt in a large bowl.
ثُمَّ عَجَنَتِ الْعَجِينَ وَخَبَزَتْهُ فِي الْفُرْنِ.
pvnvpn
Then she kneaded the dough and baked it in the oven.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى السُّوقِ قَبْلَ صَلَاةِ الْجُمُعَةِ.
vnpnpnn
The boy went to the market before the Friday prayer.
سَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ: مَا سِعْرُ الْكِيلُو؟ فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: مِائَةُ رِيَالٍ، وَهُوَ أَجْوَدُ تَمْرٍ.
vnnnnvnnnnnn
The boy asked: What is the price of a kilo? The man said: One hundred riyals, and it is the finest dates.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ حِكَايَةً: يُحْكَى أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ صَدِيقَ سُلَحْفَاةٍ.
vnpnnvpnvnn
In the rawḥa the boy read a tale: It is told that a monkey was a friend of a tortoise.
وَفِي آخِرِهَا عِبْرَةٌ لِكُلِّ صَدِيقٍ.
pnnnn
And at its end is a lesson for every friend.
ذَكَرَ الْحَبِيبُ مَثَلًا: الرَّفِيقُ قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ.
vnnnpn
The Habib mentioned a proverb: The companion before the road.
وَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِعُمَرَ: أَنْتَ رَفِيقِي فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
vnnnnpn
And the boy said to Umar: You are my companion on the road.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْوَادِي فَرَأَى نَخْلًا كَثِيرًا.
vnpnpnvnn
The boy went with his father to the wadi and saw many date palms.
وَالنَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ ثَمَرُهَا طَيِّبٌ، وَعِنْدَهَا عَيْنُ مَاءٍ.
nnnnpnn
The date palm is a tree whose fruit is good, and by it is a spring of water.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ كِتَابَ تَارِيخٍ عَنْ تَأْسِيسِ تَرِيمَ.
vnnnpnn
The boy read a history book about the founding of Tarim.
وَقَرَأَ: أُسِّسَتْ تَرِيمُ قَبْلَ وَقْتٍ طَوِيلٍ.
vvnpnn
And he read: Tarim was founded a long time ago.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي رِحْلَتِهِ: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ مَعَ أَبِي وَعُمَرَ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ.
vnpnvpnpnnvpn
The boy wrote on his journey: We left Tarim with my father and Umar, and we arrived at al-Shiḥr.
أَقَمْنَا أَيَّامًا عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَرَأَيْنَا الْمِينَاءَ.
vnpnvn
We stayed some days on the coast, and we saw the port.
فِي مُقَابَلَةٍ سَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ الْخَزَّافَ: كَيْفَ تَبْدَأُ عَمَلَكَ؟
pnvnnnvn
In an interview the boy asked the potter: How do you begin your work?
فَقَالَ الْخَزَّافُ: أَبْدَأُ بِالطِّينِ وَالْمَاءِ، وَهَذِهِ حِرْفَةُ أَبِي.
vnvnnnnn
The potter said: I begin with clay and water, and this is my father’s craft.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ عَقْدًا بَيْنَ سَالِمٍ وَعَلِيٍّ، وَكَانَ شَاهِدًا.
vnnpnnvn
The boy wrote a contract between Salim and Ali, and he was a witness.
بَاعَ سَالِمٌ لِعَلِيٍّ تَمْرًا بِثَمَنٍ قَدْرُهُ مِائَةُ رِيَالٍ.
vnnnnnnn
Salim sold dates to Ali for a price amounting to one hundred riyals.
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي صَمْتٍ عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَشَعَرَ بِفَرَحٍ وَحُزْنٍ.
vnpnpnvnn
The boy sat in silence on the coast and felt joy and sadness.
وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ: مَتَى أَرْجِعُ إِلَى أُمِّي وَإِلَى تَرِيمَ؟
vpnnvpnpn
And he said to himself: When shall I return to my mother and to Tarim?

items.en: Which two feelings does he have?

items.model: فِي نَفْسِهِ (to himself)
